newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Colombo stocks seen up on institutional buying.
newsitem.headline: Colombo stocks seen up on institutional buying.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks are seen holding their upward momentum on Thursday on higher foreign and local institutional buying, brokers said.
They said foreign funds are looking for large quantities of blue chip stocks as companies are expected to show improved results in the second quarter, and also because current price levels are low.
"There is buying pressure. Most companies are turning around after about two years and foreign and local funds are looking for big quantities," said Shanil Perera of Lanka Securities.
"Corporate results have been good and share prices are low. Hotels and manufacturing sector are looking up," he added.
Thishan Hettiarachchi of CDIC Sasson Cumberbatch stock brokers said foreign buying was likely to continue.
"Second half looks good, and new retailers are getting in. The market should move up if foreigners again become active today," he said.
The Colombo all share index ended 2.0 points higher at 776.6 on Wednesday, mostly on selective foreign buying in blue chip shares.
